author: agent
text: QUESTION (MSRV, blocks this bead): openmls =0.9.1, openmls_traits 0.6.0 and openmls_serialization_helpers 0.1.0 declare rust-version 1.91.0; the workspace declares 1.88 (JMAP-ulfy) and CI job 'msrv (1.88)' runs 'cargo +1.88.0 check --workspace --all-features --locked'. Verified locally: cargo +1.88.0 check on a probe crate depending on openmls =0.9.1 fails with 'rustc 1.88.0 is not supported by ... openmls@0.9.1 requires rustc 1.91.0'. Adding jmap-chat-mimi-server to the workspace therefore breaks the MSRV job, and inheriting rust-version.workspace (1.88) would declare a false MSRV. Options: (A) bump [workspace.package] rust-version to 1.91 and the CI msrv job to 1.91.0, record as **BREAKING** (MSRV) in CHANGELOG [Unreleased]; one constraint for all crates, but raises MSRV for consumers that never use MIMI. (B) keep workspace 1.88; give jmap-chat-mimi-server (and later -client) its own rust-version = "1.91", exclude them from the 1.88 job and add a 1.91 job for them; keeps the rest of the kit at 1.88 at the cost of a per-crate exception and a second CI job. (C) an older openmls with MSRV <= 1.88: contradicts the =0.9.1 decision and mimid's pins. Recommendation: (A). Rationale: one workspace MSRV is a constraint, while (B) is a mechanism that every later MLS crate inherits; 1.91 is about a year old as of 2026-10-20. Secondary choices I will make unless told otherwise: the backend supplies the OpenMlsCrypto provider (runtime deps stay openmls + tls_codec only); dev-deps openmls_rust_crypto =0.6.0 and openmls_basic_credential =0.6.0 (mimid's pins) generate fresh KeyPackages for the success-path tests; RFC 9420 interop vectors (passive-client-welcome.json, Basic credential 'Arnold', expired 2024-03-02) cover the reject paths. GREASE limitation of crates.io openmls filed as JMAP-6k5d.9.
